prompt: We modify Boeing 737s with DIRCM missile-protection systems for VIP/head-of-state customers. How does the new State Department rule change our ITAR posture after October 2026?
assertions: Identifies the interim final rule (91 FR 55457) revising USML Category VIII(a)(8), effective October 13, 2026
States the effect: qualifying civil aircraft (FAA transport/commuter category) modified with 'secured ASE' are excluded from the USML — the aircraft itself moves to EAR jurisdiction
Defines secured ASE correctly: DIRCM systems (or IR/UV missile-warning systems necessary for DIRCM operation) incorporated with anti-tamper measures, per new §121.0 definitions
States the critical nuance: the ASE equipment itself REMAINS on the USML in Category XI, and related technical data/defense services remain ITAR-controlled (XI(d))
Mentions the new §120.54 carve-outs: temporary import of secured ASE and country-to-country movement of previously authorized installed ASE no longer require separate authorization
